_read_this_first: NOTHING BELOW IS INVENTED. The keys in this file all begin with _ and are prose, not configuration. _this_will_not_start_the_router: This file will NOT satisfy the application. It exists so that `docker compose up` has a real file to bind-mount -- Docker silently CREATES AN EMPTY DIRECTORY at a missing bind source, which would mount a directory onto /app/fleet_config.json and fail as IsADirectoryError far from its cause. Replace the whole object when step 4 of RELEASE-SCOPE.md lands the source that reads it.
_established_from_this_repository: Mounted read-only at /app/fleet_config.json -- deploy/compose.yaml mounts it as a single FILE, not as a directory, because a directory mounted onto /app would shadow the application code.
Read by the application as Path(__file__).parent / "fleet_config.json", so it must land at that exact path (deploy/compose.yaml, deploy/README.md).

Absent from the router build context by design: deploy/images/router/Dockerfile.dockerignore does not re-admit it, and deploy/images/router/Dockerfile note 1 records that the private original baked all four in and the release cannot.
Re-read on mtime change on EVERY request, so editing the host file re-tiers a running router with no restart (deploy/compose.yaml, deploy/images/router/Dockerfile note 1, deploy/README.md).

Editing it 're-tiers' the router, so it carries the tier mapping the router routes against -- README.md's shape diagram has 'local model hosts (one or more), each serving one or more tiers' below 'classify -> tier selection -> cascade'.
The real file 'describes a specific fleet' (deploy/images/router/Dockerfile note 1), which is why the allowlist disposes it as derive-example.

_not_established: Every key name and value type EXCEPT tiers[].base_url, described below. The repository still contains no sample, loader, test or schema for this file, so nothing else here is derived from it.
Whether it is keyed by host, by tier, by model, or by something else.
What a 'tier' is named or bounded by, and what the cascade order is read from.
Whether the mtime re-read is whole-file or incremental, and what happens on a parse error mid-flight. A file re-read on every request has no restart boundary to fail at.
_placeholder_rules_for_whoever_fills_thi: Addresses: documentation range only -- 192.0.2.0/24 (RFC 5737 TEST-NET-1), or a name under example.com / example.invalid. Never a private address (10/8, 172.16/12, 192.168/16) and never a host name from the private deployment.
Never a credential, key, token or password, not even a placeholder shaped like one. If a field appears to require a real secret, that is a finding, not a value to invent.
Keep the file LF-terminated and ASCII; .gitattributes normalises *.json to LF.
The operator's copy of this file (deploy/config/<name>.json, without .example) is ignored by .gitignore on purpose: it describes a specific fleet.
_established_from_the_private_tree_NOT_f: SOURCE AND ITS WEIGHT: reported on 2026-11-02 by the session assembling the release, which can read the private tree. This repository cannot check any of it, which is why it is not filed under _established_from_this_repository. Treat it as a lead to confirm when the file lands, not as a verified schema -- the same distinction PROVENANCE in shared/resolver.py draws between a port read from an artifact that ships here and one read from an artifact that does not.
The file has 3 top-level keys, one of which is a `tiers` list.
Each entry in `tiers` carries a `base_url`: a full scheme://host:port URL with an explicit port. Reported as matching ^https?://[^/]+:\d+$ in both copies seen.
Counted 9 in the private router's copy and 10 in an older backup of it.

HOST FORM IS NOT STABLE ACROSS COPIES: the router's copy uses NAMED hosts, the older backup uses DOTTED QUADS. So any assertion that this file holds only service names would be true of one copy and false of the other. Do not write that assertion.
_this_file_is_a_second_address_surface: tiers[].base_url means the router reaches addresses that never pass through the environment or through shared/resolver.py's registry -- and because this file is re-read on mtime change, a tier's address can change under a RUNNING router with no restart and no resolution step. README.md and the resolver's docstring both claimed every address was resolved from the environment 'and nowhere else'; both were corrected on 2026-11-02. Whoever fills this in should decide whether that is the intended design or a surface to fold into the registry, and RELEASE-SCOPE.md records the question rather than answering it here.
